vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-4176
vulnerability.description: Perl heap overflow; fixed upstream in 5.43.9 / 5.42.2-rc1 / 5.40.4-rc1

statements.impact_statement: nixpkgs applies the upstream fix as a source patch without a version bump: pkgs/development/interpreters/perl/interpreter.nix references CVE-2026-4176 on nixos-26.05 and nixos-unstable (backported via NixOS/nixpkgs PR #528021). The perl 5.42.0 shipped in these images is built from that patched expression, so the version-only match is a false positive. NOT valid for images built from nixos-25.05/25.11, which never received the backport — this statement was added together with the base ref bump to nixos-26.05.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-13221
vulnerability.description: Perl regexp memory corruption with large tries (Perl/perl5 GH #23388); nixpkgs ships 5.42.0 without the guard on every channel

statements.impact_statement: Scoped to the tracelabs profile ONLY; deliberately not catalog-wide. Verified against the PUBLISHED image registry.gitlab.com/kasm-technologies/labs-sandbox/kasm-nix/tracelabs-osint:nix (config digest 1ebf3c002d76187b432dd9707278f8f4718e77e5abfb604ed4a5b59e0c2804fa, built 2026-08-03, nixpkgs rev 531670d871c0e29724a02f3cbcac170adc65b58c), pulled and inspected on a separate host rather than inferred from the build. TWO INDEPENDENT GROUNDS, both established empirically. (1) REMEDIATED where perl is compiled against. exiftool ships as /nix/store/m4wc48yxm0cxiip44pyplspwgpxf6l2q-perl5.42.0-Image-ExifTool-13.59 — the kasm-overlay build, not nixpkgs' vv9414ga550zi3b4n1my6bhrbx8qp4h6 — and its shebang resolves to /nix/store/yp5hpzyy1b73b134jhm20avjhgmyj3py-perl-5.42.0, which carries the upstream fix (Perl/perl5 03f74bbb, GH #23388). Run inside the shipped image, the exact upstream reproducer exits rc=0 on that interpreter while the image's other interpreter (haxjvirj4hk92rpjhx0qygqsf3a5iimz-perl-5.42.0) exits rc=255 with "regexp memory corruption" — so the remediation is demonstrated in the artifact, and the unpatched interpreter is demonstrated still defective, which is what makes ground (2) load-bearing rather than decorative. (2) NOT REACHABLE on the unpatched interpreter. Triggering the defect requires BOTH a fixed-string alternation exceeding U16_MAX regnodes AND regex debugging enabled. The pragma requirement was verified independently rather than taken from the upstream report: stock perl 5.42.0 runs the reproducer clean without it at reproducer size, at 4x that size, and with a single huge alternation. The pragma is NOT treated as a security boundary — PERL5OPT=-Mre=Debug reproduces the crash without editing any script (verified) — so this rests on the ABSENCE OF A QUALIFYING ALTERNATION. EVERY perl script in the image was audited, not a sample: all 73 executables with a perl shebang were compiled with `perl -c` under -Mre=Debug on the interpreter each actually runs on, which forces every literal regex through the trie path. Result: 73 CLEAN, 0 CORRUPTION, 0 INCONCLUSIVE. None builds an alternation dynamically (no `join "|"` in any of the 73). The audited set includes libwww-perl (lwp-request, lwp-download, lwp-mirror, lwp-dump), File-MimeInfo (mimeopen, mimetype), XML-Twig (xml_grep), IO-Compress (streamzip, zipdetails), Archive-Zip (crc32), IO-Compress-Brotli (bro-perl), kasmvnc's kasmvncserver plus its 16 bundled KasmVNC modules, the xdg-screensaver perl one-liner, and the ~20 perl core tools (json_pp, perldoc, prove, pod2*, cpan, piconv, ...). The audit ran with a CONTROL CANARY on the same interpreter in the same container immediately before each check, which reproduced the defect (corruption=1) every time — so a CLEAN verdict means the check could fire and did not, not that the check was inert. CORRECTION OF RECORD: an earlier revision of this statement asserted that the runtime perl consumers were kasmvnc, xdg-utils and exiftool and that "nothing else in this image reaches perl at runtime". That was WRONG — it enumerated packages reached by `nix why-depends`, not perl SCRIPTS present in the closure, and missed 70 of them. The conclusion survived the wider audit, but the original evidence did not support the original claim. RESIDUAL, stated rather than omitted: `perl -c` compiles literal regexes and `use`d modules, but NOT regexes assembled at runtime from data. No script in the image constructs an alternation via join, and the interpolations that do exist are single scalars (e.g. $host, $window_id, $defaultVisualId); an attacker would need to control such a value AND enable the pragma, both of which require already holding the privileges of the process being attacked (same-user; terminal access is already granted in this image). No privilege boundary is crossed. This is a boundary argument, not a proof of impossibility. NOT VALID for other profiles. inkscape reaches perl through enchant -> hspell -> bin/multispell, whose regexes have NOT been examined, and perl 5.42.0 is the same store path in both — only the profile scope separates them. Upstream GH #23388 remains OPEN: commit 03f74bbb declines to build an overflowing trie rather than repairing the 16-bit field. CVE severity and the first upstream release carrying the guard were NOT verified here and must be checked against NVD / perl5 release notes before use in any customer-facing risk statement.
